gloss: to cut down (a tree); to fell

definitions.gloss: to cut down (a tree); to fell
definitions.explanation: To cut through the base of a tree (or similar standing object) so that it falls over. Used both for forestry work and for removing individual trees in gardens or construction sites.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{木|き}を{切|き}り{倒|たお}した。
examples.english: I cut down the tree in the garden.

examples.japanese: {危険|きけん}な{枯|か}れ{木|き}を{切|き}り{倒|たお}す{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to cut down the dangerous dead tree.

examples.japanese: {道路|どうろ}{工事|こうじ}のために{何本|なんぼん}もの{木|き}が{切|き}り{倒|たお}された。
examples.english: Many trees were cut down for the road construction.

notes:
Compound of {切|き}る (to cut) + {倒|たお}す (to knock over). Transitive godan verb. Implies cutting all the way through so the tree topples, in contrast to mere pruning or trimming.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive — takes a direct object marked with を: {木|き}を{切|き}り{倒|たお}す.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {木|き}を{切|き}り{倒|たお}す: to fell a tree
- {森林|しんりん}を{切|き}り{倒|たお}す: to cut down a forest
- チェーンソーで{切|き}り{倒|たお}す: to fell with a chainsaw

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {伐採|ばっさい}する: to log; to fell — more technical, used for forestry
- {切|き}る: to cut — general; doesn't imply the tree falls
- {剪定|せんてい}する: to prune — trimming branches, not cutting down the tree
